WHAT THIS IS. Step 2 of .plans/grounded-llm-environment-narration/t9h-drain-condition-experiment-design.md (read sections 3, 4 and 7 first). It calibrates a typed Jev yes/no question (type `noul`, built like storygame/runtime/jev_questions.py `_noul_question`) that judges one NARRATED turn: does the narration stay inside what the world declares for a thing, or does it state that the thing is open/ajar/lifted/entered or show what is inside it without authorization? Model the whole probe (modes --validate, --dry-run, --run --confirm, --report, SHA-256 lock, redaction, the Jev client use, stop rules, row format) on scripts/ringer/environment_narration/drain_replay_probe.py and j1c_wiring_probe.py, and the wrapper on enforce_t9h_drain_replay.sh (local worker on port 8809 with --max-usd 0.06, output directory bench/results/environment-narration/t9h-drain-condition/step2, refuse if rows exist or the port is busy). Add a mode `--build-cases` that writes the frozen cases and lock (run it yourself once).

CASES. 140, from the two adjudicated, hash-frozen files: bench/results/environment-narration/t9h-drain-condition/corpus/corpus-adjudicated.json (100 drain rows; each row's `final_label` has opens_or_enters_drain, invents_ajar_or_cover_state, asserts_definite_contents; `forbidden` = any of those three) and .../heldout/heldout-labeled.json (40 labelable non-drain rows with `forbidden`, `thing`, `command`, `declared_state`, `engine_opened`; use the REAL narration text and the real thing name, not the sheet's [thing] mask). Case fields: id, set (`drain` or `heldout`), thing, command, narration, declared (a neutral sentence you render, below), forbidden (bool, the frozen label), source_ref. Drain cases: thing `storm drain`, command `inspect the storm drain`, engine did not open it; declared = the storm drain has no open or closed value, no declared contents, and is fixed in place. Held-out cases: render declared from declared_state and engine_opened as `Declared before the turn: <thing> was <closed|open|has no open/closed value>; <N> declared item(s)<, some hidden>; <fixed in place|not fixed in place>. The engine <did|did not> open it this turn.` and NEVER pass `open_state_after` or any value derived from it to the judge (that value reflects the narration's own claim). Counts to reproduce exactly: 100 drain (54 forbidden), 40 held-out (10 forbidden); the lock holds the SHA-256 of cases.jsonl.

THREE FROZEN QUESTION VARIANTS (the question text is part of the preregistration; write each as a function returning (state, questions) like searches_underneath_payload). Orientation: the noul TRUE answer means the narration STAYS INSIDE the declared state (consistent); FALSE means it states an open, ajar, lifted, entered or contents claim the declared state does not support. Accept means median score strictly above .65 and reject means median strictly below .35, like the location verifier, so a high score means consistent. Variant A (bare): state = {narration, thing}; the question asks whether the narration says the thing is open, ajar, lifted, covered or entered, or says what is inside it, as fact. Variant B (declared-state context, the pre-declared candidate): state = {narration, thing, command, declared}; instructions say the narration is consistent when it does not state any open, ajar, lifted, covered or entered condition or any contents that the declared sentence does not support; the declared sentence says whether the engine opened it this turn, and an opening the engine performed is supported; looking at, approaching, kneeling beside, touching the outside, or wondering what might be inside are consistent. Variant C: B plus one extra instruction sentence 'A condition or contents that the declared sentence does not mention is not supported.' Use plain words at about a 12th-grade level, one idea per sentence, and no story-specific word in any variant's text except through the state fields (the instructions must work for a drawer, a truck, a laptop or a drain). Put the exact variant texts in the preregistration.

CALLS. 140 cases x 3 variants x 5 samples = 2100 calls, caps --max-calls 2100 and --max-usd 0.06 (estimate about $0.04 from the earlier probes' per-call cost; compute the ceiling the same way those probes do from token estimates and print it in --dry-run). Row fields: case id, variant, sample, score (the Jev yes probability), verdict fields as the replay probe records, and the thing/set for the report.

REPORT (--report --rows FILE --out FILE). Per variant: for each case take the MEDIAN of its 5 scores; accepted = median strictly above .65, rejected = median strictly below .35, otherwise uncertain (reported separately, never counted as rejected or accepted). Gate, frozen (decided by Brandon 2026-10-30): on the drain set at least 49 of 54 forbidden rejected and at least 42 of 46 clean accepted; on the held-out set at least 9 of 10 forbidden rejected and at least 27 of 30 clean accepted; all four must hold for Variant B, the pre-declared candidate. PASS only if Variant B passes all four with a complete run (2100 rows, no stop reason); a partial run is INCONCLUSIVE; if B fails but A or C passes, print `candidate failed; another variant passed, which is a finding for a new preregistration, not a pass`. Also print per variant: counts per set, uncertain counts, the false accepts (forbidden accepted) and false rejects by case id with thing, and the forbidden-kind breakdown for the drain set from the case labels. No threshold, label or denominator is configurable.

PREREG (.plans/.../t9h-drain-condition-judge-prereg.md, written now, stating it is FROZEN before any score exists): question, sources and their hashes, the 140-case design, the three variants verbatim, Variant B as the declared candidate, per-case median, the four-condition gate with the exact numbers 49 of 54, 42 of 46, 9 of 10 and 27 of 30, 2100 calls, cap $0.06, the stop rules, no rerun, and the limits: single-reader labels, 10 held-out forbidden cases, 70B outputs only, a stub proves nothing about judgment, and a pass shows detection on these cases only, not safety or prose quality.

TESTS: hermetic with a fake Jev ask: case build reproduces the counts; lock detects an edited case; no case or payload contains open_state_after; each variant's payload shape; dry-run counts 2100; cap refusal; --run without --confirm refuses; stop on 429 and on partial run; the report on synthetic rows covers PASS, each of the four conditions failing, the median rule with one outlier sample, uncertain handling, partial = INCONCLUSIVE, and the 'candidate failed; another variant passed' line.
